item.title: Magic: The Gathering Turns a Fan-Favorite Star Trek Character Into a Commander Staple
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: Jadzia Dax, Living Legacy is one of the Universes Beyond set’s best cards
item.content:encoded: Like many Magic: The Gathering Universes Beyond sets, the Star Trek crossover feels built for Commander. Not only does it include four preconstructed Commander decks, but it’s packed with legendary creatures and spacecraft that can serve as your Commander or neatly slot into the deck’s other 99 cards. One of the most versatile cards in the set works in several Commander archetypes but could also easily fit in Limited and competitive constructed decks. It pays tribute to one of the best Star Trek characters, while borrowing mechanics from a very different Universes Beyond set.

item.title: Amazon Officially Reveals Early Black Friday Gaming Deals
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hernandez
item.description: Cyberpunk 2077, Split Fiction, and even some GOTY contenders on Nintendo, PlayStation, and Xbox are all discounted on Amazon for Black Friday 2026.
item.content:encoded: Your calendar might mark Nov. 27 as Black Friday, but the reality is that retailers treat the entire month like a discount event. Sales for major gaming products are staggered throughout the month, as evidenced by Amazon's self-described early Black Friday deals. The online retailer has earmarked a wide range of games for every taste in these deals, from recent action titles to critical darlings and everything in between.

item.title: The 2026 Game Awards Nominations Will Spoil GTA 6 Reviews
item.dc:creator: Oli Welsh
item.description: Grand Theft Auto 6's late entry into the GOTY race is awkwardly timed for both Rockstar Games and TGA's jury
item.content:encoded: GTA 6 will be released at midnight, local to whatever region you're in, on Thursday, Nov. 19. Nominations for The Game Awards will be announced at 12 p.m. EST on Tuesday, Nov. 17. The timing of the review embargo for GTA 6 is a secret closely guarded by Rockstar's famously tight NDAs, but luckily we have plenty of clear precedent to go on.

item.title: GTA 6's Official First Updates Are Great News For Fans
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hernandez
item.description: Even GTA 6 fans who already preloaded the game have two updates to download on PS5 and Xbox
item.content:encoded: Hopefully you've still got room on your hard drive after preloading the heftyGrand Theft Auto 6 in anticipation of its impending release day. You've got at least one more thing you need to download if you want to enjoy Rockstar's open-world game the moment it goes live on Nov. 19, though. Here's what you need to know about when you can download the GTA 6 update — and what's reportedly inside.

item.title: Halo Defined a Generation of LAN Parties — Then It Killed Them
item.dc:creator: Corey Plante
item.description: As Xbox and Halo turn 25, a look back at the chaotic LAN parties that made multiplayer unforgettable — and how Halo 2 helped make gathering optional.
item.content:encoded: So old, in fact, that the upcoming 25th anniversary of the Xbox and Halo: Combat Evolved immediately made me think about the LAN parties my brother and I used to host in middle and high school. There were a dozen or so teenage boys, four TVs, and enough Ethernet cable to turn my parents’ house into a tripping hazard that could also burst into flames at any moment. I’ve played countless multiplayer games since, but none have come close to the majesty of those experiences.

item.title: Extremely Rare Pokémon Game Found 20 Years Later
item.dc:creator: Ashely Claudino
item.description: PSA Video Games confirms that a collector has unearthed a playable copy of PokéPark Fishing Rally DS, a previously lost piece of Pokémon history.
item.content:encoded: PokéPark Fishing Rally DS was a 2005 temporary fishing game obtainable through Download Play on the Nintendo DS. To play it, gamers had to get it from Download Play stations at PokéPark in Nagoya, Japan. The game would remain on their console for 12 hours or until the console was shut off. After this, it would delete itself.

item.title: 10 Most Underrated RPGs of the Past Decade
item.dc:creator: Jason Venter
item.description: Some stellar RPGs have arrived over the last decade, but their brilliance made 10 absolute gems easy to miss.
item.content:encoded: There’s something about RPGs. These games tell amazing stories players want to experience time and time again, are populated by memorable characters, and often explore deep themes — even if their heroes do tend to have memory problems, spiky hair, and swords the size of New Jersey.

item.title: Prime Video's Near-Perfect Game of Thrones Replacement Officially Arrives in 2 Months
item.dc:creator: Jake Kleinman
item.description: Time to start sharpening your bloodaxe...
item.content:encoded: A weak king rules over a cobbled-together kingdom that's already coming apart at the seams. Various heroes and villains compete and scheme to claim the throne. A new challenger rises up from across the sea, full of vengeance and bloodlust... If that sounds like the premise of Game of Thrones, well, that's because it is, but it's also the set-up for Prime Video's thrilling new action drama from one of the 21st-century's most successful (and underappreciated) showrunners.

item.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s No. 1 cause of death officially revealed
item.dc:creator: Ashley Potter
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
item.description: The most modern thing about the Zelda remake might just be its mobile app.
item.content:encoded: The Zelda: Ocarina of Timeremake has officially been out for more than two weeks, and saying its reception has been good would be an understatement. It was named the No. 2 best-selling game on the Nintendo Switch 2, with over 5.2 million copies reportedly sold less than four days after launch. Longtime Zelda fans and newcomers alike have been enjoying revisiting the 1998 classic in this remake.

item.title: Nintendo Switch 2 Is Finally Getting Capcom’s Fastest-Selling Game Ever
item.dc:creator: Jen Glennon
item.description: Monster Hunter Wilds is coming to Switch 2, just in time for the holiday season. And it's also a cool 25% off ahead of launch.
item.content:encoded: With the success of Resident Evil Requiem, Pragmata, and Onimusha: Way of the Sword, it's safe to say that Capcom has had a fantastic 2026. And the venerable developer's 2025 wasn't too shabby either. Last February, it released Monster Hunter Wilds for PlayStation 5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X. It went on to sell a whopping eight million copies in just three days, making it the company's fastest-selling game of all time. As of September 2026, Monster Hunter Wilds has sold 12.2 million copies, making it Capcom's 11th-best-selling game of all time. That number is set to go up significantly after Dec. 4, when it finallylaunches for Nintendo Switch 2.

item.title: GTA 6 Trophy Count and Full Completion Time Leaks in New Reports
item.dc:creator: Ashely Claudino
item.description: Thanks to animal studies and RNG-based achievements, completionists will have to spend hundreds of hours in Grand Theft Auto 6 to 100% the game.
item.content:encoded: Millions of players will start their adventure in Leonida with the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 later this week. They're currently preparing themselves and completing the games they've left unfinished so they can dedicate all of their time to GTA 6 soon — especially gamers who have asked for time off from work to play it. But the question on many players' minds is how much time they will need to finish the story and 100% complete it.

item.title: 8 Must-Play Open-World RPGs for People With Real-Life Schedules
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Corgan
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
item.description: Busy schedule with no time to game? These eight open-world RPGs fit into short sessions, one quest or shrine at a time.
item.content:encoded: Raise your hand if this has ever happened to you: A friend texts you a screenshot of a map with 400 icons on it and the message “you’re going to love this game.” You’re excited — the map is detailed, the game looks great, and you do love it…for about 10 seconds. Until you check your calendar and remember that you’ve got a dentist appointment, three work deadlines, and a birthday dinner to prepare for, so that map is going to have to stay unexplored for a minute. (My hand is raised.)

item.title: The 2026 GOTY Race Could Be a Disaster for Indie Games
item.dc:creator: Oli Welsh
item.description: Big Walk's AI controversy might result in a step back after gains made at The Game Awards by Clair Obscur and Silksong
item.content:encoded: Some quibble with the definition of Clair Obscur, a sizable production, as an indie game. (For what it's worth, the studio that made it is independent, and its publisher Kepler Interactive was founded by a collective of indie studios; it's definitely culturally indie.) But even if you excluded it, this was still the first time more than one game had crossed over between the indie and GOTY categories in the history of the awards.

item.title: Super Meat Boy Is Officially Getting Remade Without Edmund McMillen's Involvement
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.description: The announcement of Super Meat Boy Again+ served as a reminder that Edmund McMillen is no longer part of Team Meat
item.content:encoded: Team Meat announced Super Meat Boy Again+, a remake of the classic indie platformer, during a Sweet 16 Birthday VIP Event on Nov. 14. While the announcement was meant to be celebratory, it has reminded people of the falling out that Super Meat Boy and Mewgenics creator Edmund McMillen has had with Team Meat, as he is not involved in the new project.

item.title: PlayStation Announces New Black Friday Deals On Hardware
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.description: The PlayStation VR2 is discounted, but the PlayStation 5 is not
item.content:encoded: Black Friday is fast approaching, so companies like Sony are already teasing the deals people can look forward to later this month. While PlayStation previously highlighted some of the games that will be discounted, it has now shared its official Black Friday hardware deals for the DualSense controller, PlayStation VR2, and more.

item.title: Xbox’s 25th Birthday Was All Over the Place
item.dc:creator: Oli Welsh
item.description: Asha Sharma and Microsoft used Xbox's 25th anniversary to say more about Doom, Wolfenstein, Halo, AI, and its heroic past
item.content:encoded: Patch Notes is a weekly newsletter bringing you the best of Polygon, sent on Fridays and published on the site on Sundays. You can subscribe here.

item.title: Stardew Valley Meets Night in the Woods in One of 2026's Scariest New Games
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.description: Village in the Shade is a horror farm sim that digs deep into the horrors of community life
item.content:encoded: I thought I knew what to expect from Village in the Shade after attending NIS America's pre-launch preview event in September. The villagers would be quirky but likeable, and things would probably get at least a little twisted, though nothing too terrible. Nippon Ichi Software's non-Disgaea games get pretty dark, as do the Labyrinth games and Yomawari. But they're dark on a small-scale, personal level, and rarely do they have something poignant to say. Village in the Shade tossed all my expectations out the window within the first few hours and, since then, has quickly rocketed up my list of the year's best games.

item.title: I Can't Wait to Ignore the Main Story of GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Jen Glennon
item.description: GTA 6's side activities like mini-golf, parachuting, and working out sound more fun than stealing cars and getting chased by the cops
item.content:encoded: It's hard to believe, but after years of waiting, we're less than a week away from the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. Tons of people are planning to take time off from work or school in order to sink their teeth into Rockstar's newest adventure. Many of them will be diving headfirst into Jason and Lucia's story, taking on high-stakes robberies to see how the couple's ascent through Vice City's underworld plays out. But for me, the "grand theft auto" of GTA 6 is actually the least intriguing element of 2026's most anticipated game. I couldn't care less about shooting people and stealing cars. I'm far more excited to explore the vast, glorious sandbox Rockstar has created.

item.title: Tomb Raider Remake Gameplay Changes Are Dividing Fans
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: The latest Tomb Raider remake gameplay deep dive gives a look at controversial RPG elements in Legacy of Atlantis
item.content:encoded: Amazon Game Studios has released the sixth installment in its behind-the-scenes series about the development of Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis. The remake of Lara Croft's original 1996 adventure is set to be released next year and will update the game for modern players. While that includes graphical improvements, the new video details gameplay changes and not everybody is happy about what was shown off.

item.title: Forget Ganon, Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Most Overlooked Boss Finally Gets Its Due
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Colantonio
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
item.description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a good reminder that the Zelda universe has more great villains than Ganon.
item.content:encoded: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is iconic for plenty of reasons, but a big part of that is thanks to its villain. Ganondorf is one of gaming’s great bad guys, a reputation that has only been enhanced by appearances in later games like Wind Waker and Tears of the Kingdom. While Ocarina of Time’s Switch 2 remake does the Demon King justice, it’s also a reminder that the Zelda series has another excellent, and far more underappreciated, foe: Twinrova.

item.title: Stephen King’s Underrated 1980 Horror Thriller Gets New Prime Video Adaptation
item.dc:creator: Aimee Hart
item.description: Stephen King fans rejoice: a Lovecraftian crime-thriller epic is on the way with Crouch End, a new miniseries from Prime Video.
item.content:encoded: Stephen King fans are eating well, with Mike Flanagan's adaptation of Carrie turning out to be a surprise hit, a second season of It: Welcome to Derry on the way, and a series based on The Dark Towerbooks in the works. But that's not all King fans can look forward to.

item.title: 10 Must-Play Co-Op Games for People With Real-Life Schedules
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Corgan
item.description: Short on time but ready to game? These 10 co-op games range from one-level sessions to month-long campaigns, from Overcooked! to Gears of War: E-Day.
item.content:encoded: Picture this: It’s Thursday at 7:42 p.m. You finally have two friends in the same voice call. Someone’s cat is walking across their keyboard, and a third friend is still stuck in a meeting, but you’re here, and you’re ready to game. There’s a problem, though: Many of today’s most popular co-op games ask a lot of their players. And often, you simply don’t have a lot of time or headspace to give. You need a co-op game that fits the time and energy you and your squad actually have.

item.title: Nintendo Officially Reveals New Kirby Game for Switch 2
item.dc:creator: Ashely Claudino
item.description: Kirby and the World Beyond is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027
item.content:encoded: HAL Laboratory's venerable heroic pink puff Kirby will soon embark on a new adventure on Nintendo Switch 2 with the release of Kirby and the World Beyond next year — his second outing on Nintendo's current-generation console. In September, Nintendo's Yoshiaki Koizumi announced Kirby's next adventure during a Nintendo Direct showcase, revealing an expansive new world for the adorable hero to explore.

item.title: League of Legends: New Dawn Revealed, Major Overhaul Set for 2027
item.dc:creator: Matt Patches
item.description: Riot Games revealed at Worlds Finals 2026 a major update to League of Legends coming in 2027 with new gameplay and features.
item.content:encoded: Between matches at the 2026 League of Legends World Championship, Riot Games teased fans with a long-anticipated announcement: The next era of League of Legends is upon us.

item.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Is Actually the Perfect Way to Introduce Kids to Nintendo
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Corgan
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
item.description: Parents are debating whether the Ocarina of Time remake is too scary for kids. Here’s the case for the child-era half as a first Nintendo game.
item.content:encoded: Walk into The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Kokiri Forest, and it feels like you’re walking into a picture book. Especially in the remake, everything is moss-green and dappled with light. Fairies flit about. Kokiri children are rhythmically attending to their tasks. Everyone is friendly, everything is beautiful, and the world both feels safe and makes sense. Then you walk into the Great Deku Tree and spiders start falling from the ceiling. My daughter screamed. I jumped, too, and I knew they were coming.

item.title: Magic Is Bringing Back Its Most Controversial Creature Type
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.description: Magic: The Gathering's Aaron Forsythe tells Polygon he knows when more Sliver cards will come to the game
item.content:encoded: Whether you love or hate Sliver decks in Magic: The Gathering, you should prepare for more Sliver cards to make their way to the game soon. Vice President of Design Aaron Forsythe revealed as much during an in-person interview with Polygon at MagicCon: Atlanta 2026.

item.title: Blade Runner Is Officially Getting The AAA Game Treatment
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.description: Alcon Entertainment confirmed it has had discussions about creating a AAA game based on Blade Runner
item.content:encoded: Alcon Entertainment, which owns the Blade Runner franchise, confirmed in a recent interview that it has discussed making a AAA game based on the beloved sci-fi series. It's an exciting development for Blade Runner, which has never quite found its footing in gaming despite how influential its visual style and narrative themes have been.

item.title: The Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Is an Event Even if You’re Not Playing It
item.dc:creator: Oli Welsh
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
item.description: Watching personal reactions to Nintendo's Switch 2 version of The Legend of Zelda: OoT is beautiful
item.content:encoded: Switchboard is Polygon's weekly newsletter for all things Nintendo, sent on Thursdays and published on the site on Saturdays. You can subscribe here.

item.title: 8 Iconic Video Game Villains Who Were Actually Right the Whole Time
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Corgan
item.description: The best video game villains of all time had motives that, when you think about them, actually made a whole lot of sense.
item.content:encoded: Grab your gavel: Court is in session for eight of gaming’s most misunderstood villains. Their charges? One occupied planet, one erased painting, one underwater utopia gone to rot, and a truly staggering body count. But, all that aside, what if these bad guys were actually making a somewhat decent point? Read between the lines of their melodramatic monologues, and perhaps you’ll realize that, say, a centuries-long guilt trip over one catastrophic mistake was in fact understandable rationale for wanting to tear the world down and start over. Or not: You get to decide. Just read each villain’s case file below before reaching a verdict — you might not love where the evidence actually points.

item.title: Ubisoft Is Reportedly Bringing A Beloved Series Back After Nearly Two Decades
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.description: A new Rainbow Six: Vegas game is in the works at Ubisoft Montreal, according to a new report
item.content:encoded: Before Rainbow Six Siege, Ubisoft published two Rainbow Six: Vegas games for PS3 and Xbox 360. Now, a new report suggests that a third Rainbow Six: Vegas game is in the works, moving the franchise beyond Siege.

item.title: Magic: The Gathering’s 5 Best and Weirdest Star Trek References
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: The set has nods to some of the franchise’s silliest moments
item.content:encoded: Magic: The Gathering’s Star Trek is a love letter to the franchise. The set uses sagas to pay tribute to standout episodes like “The Inner Light” and “In the Pale Moonlight,” and it’s stuffed with cards representing legendary characters and spacecraft along with famous quotes like “Live long and prosper.” But the set also features plenty of deeper cuts, embracing the times that Star Trek was silly, controversial, and downright terrible. These are the five best references to the franchise’s worst and weirdest moments.

item.title: Big Walk's AI Controversy Overshadows a Remarkable Creative Achievement
item.dc:creator: Matt Patches
item.description: House House's 2026 Game of the Year contender used an LLM to get over the finish line, but the run to get there was pure human craft.
item.content:encoded: And then we took Kalonica [Quigley] in, who's now the fifth member of House House, and gave her a tour of this island. It was much smaller than the final thing, but it was really just an island with a bunch of trees and a few rocks, and maybe the red lookout tower was there, or an earlier version of it. There was a giant floating sphere and maybe just some really primitive shapes. But we took her around and had this really amazing experience just exploring together. It felt social and fun, like hanging out with your friends.

item.dc:creator: Jen Glennon
item.description: Who will play Jason, Lucia, and other major characters in GTA 6? Rockstar hasn't made an official reveal yet, but the internet has plenty of ideas.
item.content:encoded: It's been an excruciatingly long wait, but we're just days away from the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. Ahead of the game's launch for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, Rockstar Games has yet to reveal any official details about the actors who will appear in GTA 6, including the central couple, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos.

item.title: Zelda Fans Who Loved Ocarina of Time Need to Play This Game Next
item.dc:creator: Jason Venter
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
item.description: Ocarina of Time features some memorable moments, and many of them were similarly compelling in a previous Zelda adventure.
item.content:encoded: By now, you’ve probably had time to play The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on the Nintendo Switch 2. You’ve marveled at what a great job it does of bringing the classic Nintendo 64 adventure to a new generation, with visual improvements and quality-of-life changes to make it more palatable for that new audience. Maybe you’ve even run through it a second time.

item.title: 20 Years Later, A Classic Nintendo DS Puzzle Game Officially Returns
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: Level-5 is remaking the classic Nintendo DS puzzle game Professor Layton and the Curious Village and it's due out in 2027
item.content:encoded: Next year will mark the 20th anniversary of Level-5's beloved Professor Layton series. To celebrate, the company has announced it is remaking Professor Layton and the Curious Village.

item.title: Fallout 5 and Fallout Remasters Officially Announced
item.dc:creator: Michael McWhertor
item.description: Bethesda Softworks updates fans on the future of Fallout, which includes new Fallout 3 and New Vegas releases and Fallout 5.
item.content:encoded: Xbox wants more Fallout, and after a yearslong drought of new games, Bethesda Softworks is making it happen. Bethesda plans to release remasters of both Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas for modern platforms, the company said in July in a massive roadmap of the developer's future. Those remasters are part of a larger plan to reinvest in Fallout games — including Fallout 5, which is currently in pre-production — and a new untitled project at Obsidian Entertainment.

item.title: Blizzard Officially Responds to Disappointed Overwatch Fans Over Hero 55
item.dc:creator: Michael McWhertor
item.description: Overwatch's next hero, Hudson, will be a Damage (DPS) character, not a support. Fans are disappointed by the switch and Blizzard is responding.
item.content:encoded: Blizzard Entertainment is about to make good on the promise of delivering 10 new heroes to Overwatch in 2026, with the final addition arriving in December. The 10th new hero coming to Overwatch in 2026 is an Omnic detective named Hudson, and he'll arrive alongside the launch of season 6. Hudson was officially revealed on Thursday, but many Overwatch fans aren't pleased with a key aspect of his character.

item.title: 6 Most-Anticipated Steam Games You Should Add to Your Wishlist Right Now
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Colantonio
item.description: The best upcoming Steam games to add to your Wishlist include an open-world RPG, a narrative adventure, and... a game about slaps?
item.content:encoded: Sometimes when we put together a new installment of Wishlister, Polygon’s weekly newsletter that highlights upcoming Steam games, we look to events like Steam Next Fest and the Triple-I Initiative to dig up gems. But the most tried-and-true method we’ve found for finding promising games is simply stumbling into them by accident.

item.title: Cities: Skylines' Best Replacement Is Finally Here and Better than Expected
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.description: Transport Fever 3 turned me into a lover of logistics-based city builder games with how much more hands-on it is compared to Cities: Skylines
item.content:encoded: 2026 is the year I got massively into city builders, and by massively I mean I played Cities: Skylines more than anything else for the first half of the year. I started dabbling with city builder-slash-logistics games in the second half of the year, like Anno 117, and turned my attention to Transport Fever 3 soon after. When I first learned about Transport Fever 3, I called it "like" Cities: Skylines. It looked a lot like a traditional city builder, albeit one where you focus on roads more than zoning. After playing it over the last month or so, though, I realize the difference between city builder and logistics planner is a lot more distinct than I initially gave it credit for — and I've irreversibly become a logistics sicko.

item.title: 8 New TV Shows to Watch This Weekend on Netflix, Prime Video, and HBO (November 13-15)
item.dc:creator: Maria Loreto
item.category: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power
item.description: On this week's TV column, there's the return of one of the biggest fantasy franchises in the world, a new Netflix horror, and more.
item.content:encoded: It’s a big weekend for new TV. VisionQuesthas concluded its first season, including a post-credits scene with big implications for Avengers: Doomsday. The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power is back with a third season, continuing the story of a Middle-earth set thousands of years before Bilbo and Frodo Baggins. The Body is also available on Netflix, delivering a fun and campy high school drama with some religious horror thrown in the mix.

item.title: Blood of Dawnwalker Finally Gets Its Most Requested Feature Next Week
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: Blood of Dawnwalker update 1.2 will add New Game + next week after overwhelming fan demand
item.content:encoded: It's been just over two months since The Blood of Dawnwalker was released and fans have been clamoring for one missing feature for basically that long. Now developer Rebel Wolves is set to appease that demand with the upcoming update 1.2. Yes, New Game Plus is going to be a reality for the vampire RPG.

item.title: The Game Awards 2026 Nominees Announcement Confirmed for Nov. 17
item.dc:creator: Michael McWhertor
item.description: Geoff Keighley's The Game Awards will announce 2026's nominees, including Game of the Year, on Tuesday, Nov. 17.
item.content:encoded: The Game Awards 2026 is approaching, and this year's award nominees are set to be announced on Tuesday, Nov. 17. That's according to host and creator of The Game Awards Geoff Keighley, who announced Friday that 2026's nominees will be revealed during a livestream — that just happens to be coming two days ahead of the year's most anticipated game, Grand Theft Auto 6.

item.title: Every Free Game You Can Keep on Steam, Epic, PlayStation Plus, and Xbox (Nov. 13-19)
item.dc:creator: Ashely Claudino
item.description: Epic Games Store, Steam, and Xbox have some free games to keep you busy before GTA 6 drops.
item.content:encoded: Next week the world will stop for many players with the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. If you've already preloaded GTA 6, then you'll be ready to hit "Play" as soon as it becomes available on Nov. 19. In the meantime, you have to find a game that'll keep you busy.

item.title: Magic Just Revealed 19 New Cards From 2027’s First Set — Including a $30 Reprint With Stunning Art
item.dc:creator: Corey Plante
item.description: Wizards of the Coast gave Nauctis: The Sunken Realm a proper introduction at MagicCon: Atlanta.
item.content:encoded: Magic: The Gathering is heading underwater, and we’ve just gotten a closer look at what’s lurking in the depths of a new plane called Nauctis. During Friday’s preview panel at MagicCon: Atlanta, Wizards of the Coast revealed 19 cards from Nauctis: The Sunken Realm (including different art variants), the upcoming set that introduces an ocean plane to Magic’s Multiverse. Launching on Feb. 5, 2027, the set trades typical fantasy settings like Dominaria or Ikoria for sprawling underwater cities and aquatic creatures, with greater dangers waiting farther below the surface.

item.title: The 25 Best Switch 2 Games
item.dc:creator: Oli Welsh
item.description: The best Nintendo Switch 2 games include Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and plenty more.
item.content:encoded: That's in addition to stellar third-party support, with almost unanimous buy-in from indies and several big publishers going all-in on porting their biggest titles to Switch 2 — notably Square Enix, with the Final Fantasy 7 series, and Capcom, with Resident Evil, Onimusha, Pragmata, and more coming.
